dimensions.assessment: Affects businesses and individuals engaged in international trade and subject to U.S. export control regulations, as well as federal enforcement agencies.
dimensions.evidence: increases civil penalties for violations of U.S. export control laws.

dimensions.assessment: Substantial effect on parties committing violations because the maximum penalty per violation increases significantly from $300,000 (or twice the transaction value) to $1.2 million (or four times the transaction value).
dimensions.evidence: increases the maximum statutory civil penalty for each violation... to $1.2 million or four times the value of the transaction

dimensions.assessment: Potential increase in federal revenue from civil penalties collected, though the exact total amount depends on future enforcement actions and violations.
Directly amends a specific section of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 regarding penalty amounts without creating new regulatory agencies or broad programs.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to increase the civil penalties that may be imposed under such Act.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change applicable to violations committed on or after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: shall apply with respect to a violation of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018... committed on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The source does not estimate how many violations occur annually or the total projected increase in federal fine collections.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill quadruples the statutory maximum civil penalties for violations of U.S. export control laws under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018, changing liability for entities violating export controls.
